origin: it ignores `use` statements for modules not ending in 'Case'
source:
defmodule FooTest do
  use SomeModule
end

origin: it allows `use MyApp.DataCase, async: true`
source:
defmodule FooTest do
  use MyApp.DataCase, async: true
end

origin: it allows `use MyApp.DataCase, async: false`
source:
defmodule BlahTest do
  use MyApp.DataCase, async: false
end

origin: it allows `use MyApp.DataCase, async: false` with a commit
source:
defmodule FooTest do
  # a comment explaining why async is false
  use MyApp.DataCase, async: false
end

origin: it allows `use MyApp.DataCase, async:` with a value from a function call
source:
defmodule FooTest do
  use MyApp.DataCase, async: Application.compile_env(:my_app, :async, true)
end

origin: it allows `use MyApp.DataCase, async:` with a value from an attribute
source:
defmodule FooTest do
  @async false
  use MyApp.DataCase, async: @async
end

origin: it does not allow `use MyApp.DataCase` with other options but not `async:`
source:
defmodule ThingTest do
  use MyApp.DataCase, bite_strength: :xtreme
end

findings.message: Pass an `:async` boolean option to `use` a test case module.

origin: it does not allow `use MyApp.DataCase` without options
source:
defmodule FooTest do
  # some comment
  use MyApp.DataCase
end

findings.message: Pass an `:async` boolean option to `use` a test case module.

origin: it does not allow `use MyApp.DataCase` with `async: false`
source:
defmodule FooTest do
  use MyApp.DataCase, async: false
end

findings.message: Tests with `async: false` need a comment explaining why they can't be run asynchronously.
